newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso move needed to defend economy-Ramos.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso move needed to defend economy-Ramos.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos said on Friday the Philippine decision to allow greater peso exchange rate flexibility was a "decisive action" needed to defend the country's economic gains.

"This exchange rate action reaffirms the goverment's commitment to do whatever is necessary to sustain our economic growth, control inflation and generate employment through, among others, the protection of our international reserves," Ramos said in a statement.

"This decisive action of the Monetary Board protects the well-earned economic gains of the Filipino people from the effects of the current difficult circumstances prevailing in regional markets," he said.

The Central Bank said earlier on Friday it would allow the peso to move in a wider range against the U.S. dollar. The move follows pressure on the peso after the Thai government devalued its baht currency on July 2.
The peso tumbled about 11.5 percent to 29.45 per dollar at the start of Asian trade and the Bankers Association of the Philippines halted dealings for the day.
